title: Token cost allocation heatmap + exportable pricing pattern library
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Design a new console surface that visualizes token-level cost allocation as a multi-layer heatmap and bundles a small library of exportable pricing patterns. The heatmap should let engineers and finance teams quickly understand where tokens are being spent across routes, models, and customer segments. This ticket covers low-fidelity exploration, an interactive prototype, export schema proposals (ledger-friendly CSV and pivot-ready JSON), and a short design spec for frontend/analytics implementation.
goals: Surface per-route and per-model per-token cost hotspots with color-graded intensity
Expose amortized cost layers (inference infra, caching savings, spot vs reserved) as toggles
Provide 2 export modes: detailed ledger CSV for billing ingestion and summarized pivot JSON for analytics teams
Ship a compact ‘pricing pattern’ preview that demonstrates effects of slab vs microcost pricing on real workloads
constraints: Must work with existing Console metrics backend and token attribution traces
Export formats limited to CSV/JSON for initial release (no parquet yet)
UI must perform acceptably with 200+ routes in a single view (virtualize rows)
Design must accommodate Dedicated and Private deployments where some fields are redacted for privacy
acceptance_criteria: Interactive Figma prototype shows heatmap with route/model axes, hover card with per-token breakdown and attribution links
Export button produces sample CSV and JSON schemas attached to this ticket and approved by PM
Pricing pattern preview demonstrates delta between per-token and slab pricing with adjustable knobs and previews monthly estimate
Frontend implementation notes contain clear mapping of heatmap cells to backend metrics and required new APIs
Design has received sign-off from PM (Raj Patel) and eng reviewer (Anita Gupta) and no unresolved blockers from Security
design_decisions: Use a 5-color sequential scale for heat intensity; reserve red for top 1% of spenders to avoid alarm fatigue
Rows: route; Columns: model variant (fallback and canary variants shown side-by-side)
Each cell shows three micro-rows on hover: token_count, amortized_cost, cache_savings
Export CSV to use long format with columns: date, route, model_variant, token_type, token_count, unit_cost, infra_amortized, cache_savings, total_cost
Pricing preview uses sample 30-day window and extrapolates based on median daily usage to reduce noise
